name: Cognition
tagline: The autonomous coding-agent lab that went from Devin's launch to a US$48B valuation in 18 months
shortSummary: Cognition is the San Francisco lab behind Devin, the first fully autonomous AI software engineer, founded in late 2023 by IOI-gold-medallist competitive programmers.

facts.label: Founders
facts.value: Scott Wu (CEO); Steven Hao (CTO); Walden Yan (CPO) — IOI gold medallists

facts.label: Sector
facts.value: Autonomous AI software engineering (Devin) + AI-native IDE (Windsurf)

facts.label: Flagship products
facts.value: Devin (autonomous agent); Windsurf IDE; Devin Desktop (2026)

rounds.label: Seed
rounds.note: Disclosed the same day Devin launched publicly, led by Founders Fund. The launch post described it as a 'Series A,' but later reporting re-classified it as the seed once the larger ~US$175M round closed within weeks. Valuation not disclosed.

rounds.label: Series A
rounds.note: Reported by The Information/Bloomberg/Forbes weeks after Devin's launch; Founders Fund re-led. Cognition did not publish a separate blog post for this round.

rounds.label: Series B
rounds.note: Reported March 2025 round at approximately a US$4B post-money valuation, jointly led by Lux Capital and 8VC. Amount undisclosed; the Lux + 8VC co-lead is later confirmed by Scott Wu's September 2025 post.

rounds.label: Series C
rounds.note: Confirmed via Scott Wu's blog; led by Founders Fund. Closed about two months after the Windsurf acquisition.

rounds.label: Series D
rounds.note: Confirmed via Cognition's 'More Devins in More Places' post: >US$1B at a US$25B pre-money / US$26B post-money valuation. Alongside the round Cognition disclosed US$492M run-rate revenue with enterprise usage up over 10x since the start of 2026.

rounds.label: Series E
rounds.note: Led by new investors Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, with 30+ more firms participating. Run-rate revenue rose from US$492M to nearly US$900M since the May round; the valuation nearly doubled in four months. Notably a16z — a major Cursor backer — led a round in Cursor's direct competitor.

sections.heading: From IOI Gold Medals to Devin's Launch
sections.body: The three co-founders — competitive-programming champions with ten IOI gold medals between them — launched Devin in March 2024 as 'the first AI software engineer,' an agent that plans, codes, debugs and deploys end to end inside its own IDE, shell and browser. The launch post carried a US$21M Founders Fund-led round and a who's-who of angels (the Collisons, Elad Gil, Sarah Guo), and within weeks a ~US$175M Series A at ~US$2B made it one of the fastest unicorns in AI history.

sections.heading: The Revenue Ramp That Defies AI-coding Skeptics
sections.body: Devin's disclosed run-rate went from US$1M (September 2024) to US$73M (June 2025) — 73x in nine months. The July 2025 Windsurf acquisition added another ~US$82M ARR and an AI-native IDE; by the Series D (May 2026) company-wide run-rate hit US$492M, and by the Series E (September 2026) it neared US$900M. Cognition is reportedly targeting US$4–5B annualized revenue by end-2026, though it still operates at a loss with compute and server leasing estimated near US$800M a year.

sections.heading: Windsurf, and the Parallel Google Deal
sections.body: Cognition's July 2025 acquisition of the Windsurf IDE (formerly Codeium) was the deal that folded a rival coding tool's enterprise base into Devin — while, about a week earlier, Google executed a separate ~US$2.4B 'reverse-acquihire' taking Windsurf's CEO and ~40 senior R&D staff to Google DeepMind. Cognition got the product, IP, ~US$82M ARR and ~200 employees; Google got the founding leadership. Two more acqui-hires followed in July 2026 (TierZero, then The Interaction Company's Poke).

sections.heading: Enterprise Proof Points as the Moat
sections.body: Cognition's named customers span the most demanding organizations: Mercedes-Benz (whose pilot cut a COBOL modernization from eight months to eight days), NASA JPL, Goldman Sachs, Citi, the U.S. Army and Navy, Dell, Palantir, Santander, Itaú. FedRAMP High In-Process status and a DOE Genesis Mission MOU underscore the federal/regulated wedge — the harder-to-replicate layer that distinguishes Devin from consumer coding tools.

sections.heading: A Valuation Priced as Infrastructure
sections.body: The Series E's US$48B against ~US$900M run-rate implies a ~53x multiple — the territory where investors price category dominance, not incremental growth. The round's lead is the subplot: a16z, a major Cursor backer that profited from its SpaceX sale, led a round in Cursor's direct competitor, signaling that AI coding is seen as far from winner-take-all and that autonomous agents have crossed from productivity tool to infrastructure layer.
